title: An inverse-protein-folding pre-trained model for predicting the mutational effects in protein-protein interactions.
authors: Mao, Sihong; Meng, Siwei; Xiang, Ye
one_liner_zh: 该文提出基于逆折叠预训练的消息传递神经网络DGMPNN，用于预测蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用中突变引起的结合亲和力变化，属于蛋白质结构相关的AI计算建模，与课题高度相关。
abstract: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) are fundamental to vast biological processes. Accurate prediction of mutation-induced changes in PPIs is crucial for protein engineering and drug discovery. Most existing PPI prediction approaches rely on refined physicochemical features or computationally intensive structural sampling. Here, we present delta-G message-passing-neural-network (DGMPNN), a message-passing neural-network framework for predicting the effects of mutations on PPIs. DGMPNN is pre-trained on an inverse protein folding (IPF) task and employs an adaptive residue-level attention pooling mechanism to enable effective transfer learning for predicting mutation-induced changes in protein binding affinity. The model achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmark datasets and deep mutational scanning (DMS) datasets. Experimental validation using computationally selected multi-site variants of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD-hACE2 complex showed strong agreement between predicted and experimentally measured binding affinities.
abstract_zh: 蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPIs）是广泛生物学过程中的基础。准确预测突变引起的PPIs变化对于蛋白质工程和药物发现至关重要。现有的大多数PPI预测方法依赖于精细的物理化学特征或计算密集的结构采样。在此，我们提出了delta-G消息传递神经网络（DGMPNN），一种用于预测突变对PPIs影响的消息传递神经网络框架。DGMPNN在逆向蛋白质折叠（IPF）任务上进行了预训练，并采用自适应残基级注意力池化机制，以实现有效的迁移学习，用于预测突变引起的蛋白质结合亲和力变化。该模型在多个基准数据集和深度突变扫描（DMS）数据集上达到了最先进的性能。使用计算选择的多位点SARS-CoV-2 RBD-hACE2复合物变体的实验验证显示，预测与实验测得的结合亲和力之间具有强烈的一致性。
